couchcoop_qr_no_address: No host address available — check the browser server started.
couchcoop_qr_network_connection_descript: Choose the network this PC uses to reach your phone. PC name (.local) uses the computer’s name instead of an interface address.
couchcoop_qr_copy_link_description: Copies this address to your clipboard, so you can paste it into a chat message or type it into a phone's browser.
couchcoop_steam_offline: Steam offline — remote friends can't join. Couch/LAN play only.
couchcoop_couch_seats_unavailable: Couch players can't join — another program is using the port they need. Close any other copy of Slay the Spire 2, then host again.
couchcoop_host_transport_not_started: Couch players can't join because CouchCoop did not see this lobby's game host start. Return to the main menu and host again. If this repeats, copy a connection report.
couchcoop_option_server_not_listening: The browser server is not listening yet.
couchcoop_option_address_not_eligible: Needs a normal network address on this PC.
couchcoop_option_secure_pending: Still setting up — the plain address still works.
couchcoop_secure_idle: Select to set up the HTTPS link. Internet access may be needed.
couchcoop_secure_address_ineligible: Needs a normal network address on this PC.
couchcoop_secure_port_failed: Could not open the secure port.
couchcoop_secure_setup_failed: Setup failed — the plain address still works.
couchcoop_secure_provider_unavailable: No internet, or the certificate service is down.
couchcoop_secure_certificate_key_mismatc: The published certificate and key do not match.
couchcoop_secure_certificate_not_valid_y: The published certificate is not valid yet.
couchcoop_secure_certificate_expired: The published certificate has expired — it usually returns within a day.
couchcoop_secure_certificate_load_failed: This PC could not load the published certificate.
couchcoop_qr_adapter_ethernet_descriptio: This PC is plugged in with a cable — the steadiest option, with the least lag. Your phone still joins over Wi-Fi, but the PC's half of the connection is as good as it gets.
couchcoop_qr_adapter_wifi_description: This PC is on Wi-Fi. It works, but it's less stable than a cable — expect a little more lag or stutter, especially far from the router. If the PC also has a wired option, prefer that.
couchcoop_qr_adapter_other_description: A VPN or virtual network (a work VPN, a virtual machine, and the like). Only phones on that same network can use this address — on normal home Wi-Fi, pick one of the options above instead.
couchcoop_qr_method_ipv4_description: A simple local link that needs no internet or certificate setup. It uses HTTP, so some browser features are unavailable. To enable secure browser features, choose an HTTPS method.
couchcoop_qr_method_web_description: Loads from the internet, then connects to this PC. Your browser may ask for local-network access; the site can reach programs that explicitly accept its connections, like this game. HTTPS enables additional browser features. Needs internet on the device and does not work on iPhone yet.
couchcoop_qr_method_secure_description: An HTTPS link straight to this PC using a domain name. Enables additional browser features without installing this PC’s certificate. Needs internet. Some routers or internet providers block this address; if it will not load, choose another method.
couchcoop_qr_method_mdns_description: Uses this PC's name instead of numbers — easy to remember and type by hand. But many phones and routers can't find these names, so it's the least reliable option. If it won't load, use one of the addresses above.
couchcoop_qr_method_override_description: This address was pinned by the COUCHCOOP_ADVERTISED_HOST setting on this PC, so the dialog shows exactly what was configured.
couchcoop_qr_mdns_untrusted_suffix: Heads up: this name didn't answer when we tested it on your network just now.
couchcoop_connection_copy_failed: Couldn't verify the clipboard. Select Copy report and try again.
couchcoop_connection_error_launch_summar: The player game could not start.
couchcoop_connection_error_host_no_couch: Players on this computer can't join this lobby.
Close any other copy of Slay the Spire 2 running on this computer, then host again.
couchcoop_connection_error_host_transpor: Players on this computer can't join this lobby.
Return to the main menu and host again. If it still fails, copy this report.
couchcoop_connection_error_join_summary: The player game lost its connection.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_run_in_p: The run has already started, so this player's game cannot join it.
Reload the saved run to let this player back in.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_content_: This player's game loaded different game content than the host.
A mod failed to load, or loaded differently, in this player's game. Check that player's own log (its path is in this report) for mod errors, then try again.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_mod_mism: This player's game loaded a different set of mods than the host.
A mod failed to load, or is missing, in this player's game. Check that player's own log (its path is in this report) for mod errors, then try again.
couchcoop_connection_error_mod_mismatch_: This player's game loaded a different copy of CouchCoop.
Keep only one copy of the mod installed, restart the game, then try again.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_cloud_is: This player's game could not promise to leave your Steam Cloud saves alone.
It was stopped. Restart the game and try again, and copy this report if it happens again.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_silent_s: This player's game started and joined, then stopped responding.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_silent_a: Try again. If it keeps happening, check that player's own log (its path is in this report) and try again with other mods disabled.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_control_: This player's game is running, but it cannot report back to your game.
Allow Slay the Spire 2 through this computer's firewall and security software, turn off any VPN, proxy or network-filtering software on this computer, then try again.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_relay_su: The shared port could not reach this player’s game view.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_relay_ac: Retry the connection. If this keeps happening, restart the host game.
couchcoop_connection_error_host_browser_: Another program on this computer is using the configured browser port.
Free that port, then restart the host game.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_port_sum: Another program on this computer is using this player's port.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_port_act: Close whatever is using that port on the host computer, including another copy of Slay the Spire 2, then try again.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_port_occ: Another program on this computer is using one of the ports Couch Co-Op gives players.
Co-op still works. Players are routed around that port. Close the other program if a player later cannot connect.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_port_blo: This computer is blocking the port this player's game is serving on.
Allow Slay the Spire 2 through this computer's firewall or security software, then try again.
couchcoop_connection_error_seat_network_: This player's game is running, but their device never reached it.
Allow Slay the Spire 2 through this computer's firewall and security software, check the device is on this computer's network and not a guest one, then scan the code again.
couchcoop_connection_error_browser_summa: The browser could not show the game view.
couchcoop_connection_error_browser_actio: Reload the browser, then join again.
couchcoop_connection_error_service_actio: Return to the lobby and try again.
couchcoop_connection_error_patch_summary: Couch Co-Op could not attach to the game, so co-op cannot run this session.
couchcoop_connection_error_patch_action: Restart the game. If co-op still does not start, copy this report.
couchcoop_connection_error_shared_profil: Players on this computer share one game profile.
Co-op still works. Avoid changing game settings while other players are connected.
couchcoop_connection_error_reachability_: No phone or browser has connected to this PC yet.

If nobody has tried yet, this is normal. If someone is trying and it times out, check their phone is on this same network, then let this game accept incoming connections - on macOS under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network and System Settings > Network > Firewall; on Windows, in the firewall prompt for the game.
couchcoop_connection_error_host_firewall: This computer's firewall is blocking players from connecting.

Allow Slay the Spire 2 through Windows Firewall as a program (not a port), with Private ticked, and delete any block rule an earlier prompt left behind. Copy this report for the exact rule this PC found.
couchcoop_connection_empty: Devices appear here after connecting to the browser server. Use the same Wi-Fi network and check the address shown above.
couchcoop_connection_error_slow_summary: Waiting for the browser to display the game.
couchcoop_connection_error_slow_action: Keep this tab open. Reload it if loading does not finish.
couchcoop_connection_outcome_detail_wait: Still waiting for the game view. This attempt can still finish.
couchcoop_connection_outcome_detail_fail: This attempt stopped. Follow the suggested steps, then reconnect.
couchcoop_connection_outcome_detail_reco: The game view is now working. This earlier warning is saved for reference.
couchcoop_connection_outcome_detail_ende: This connection ended before the delay cleared.
couchcoop_connection_outcome_detail_degr: Co-op is running with a limitation. It is saved here for reference.
couchcoop_seatmods_purpose: If a mod crashes browser players' games, turn it off for them here.
couchcoop_seatmods_visuals: They'll see the game without it, including its visuals.
couchcoop_seatmods_declared: Only mods whose authors say they don't change gameplay are listed. That's the author's word, not a guarantee.
couchcoop_seatmods_applies_to_new: Changes apply to players who join from now on. Anyone already connected keeps the mods they joined with.
couchcoop_seatmods_detail_locked: {mod} stays on because {dependent} needs it, and {dependent} changes gameplay.
couchcoop_seatmods_detail_off_with: {mod} is off because it needs {mods}. Turn {mods} back on to bring it back.
couchcoop_seatmods_confirm_prompt: Turning off {mod} also turns off the mods that need it: {mods}.
couchcoop_qr_method_selector_description: Choose how devices connect to this PC. Direct address (HTTPS), Website, and Domain name use HTTPS, which enables additional browser features. Each option explains its setup and network requirements.
couchcoop_qr_method_requires_interface: Select a network interface with an eligible IP address to use this method.
couchcoop_qr_website_unconfigured: No website is configured for this method.
couchcoop_qr_method_direct_https_descrip: An HTTPS link straight to this PC using its IP address. Needs no hostname or internet. Each device needs one-time certificate setup. Selecting this method opens the guide; the setup button opens it again afterward.
couchcoop_direct_https_pending: Set up HTTPS to show your QR code. Use the setup button to open the guide.
couchcoop_direct_https_ready: This PC is ready. Each player’s device still needs to install and trust its security certificate.
couchcoop_direct_https_failed: Setup could not finish. Try again. For an expired or damaged certificate, open Help & advanced.
couchcoop_direct_https_authority_expired: This PC’s security certificate has expired. Open Help & advanced → Reset setup, then install the new certificate on every device.
couchcoop_direct_https_authority_invalid: This PC’s saved security certificate is damaged. Open Help & advanced → Reset setup, then install the new certificate on every device.
couchcoop_direct_https_warning: Trust only a host you control. Installing its CA lets this PC certify other websites too, not just this game. Keep its private keys private.
couchcoop_direct_https_transfer: 1. Prepare this host. 2. Export the PUBLIC certificate. Transfer the .cer file by cable or authenticated file transfer. Compare its full SHA-256 fingerprint with the value below. Never obtain trust material through an unverified HTTP download. 3. Install trust on each client, then scan the HTTPS QR.
couchcoop_direct_https_platforms: iPhone/iPad: install the profile in Settings → General → VPN & Device Management, then enable it in General → About → Certificate Trust Settings. Android: Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate (names vary). Windows: import into Trusted Root Certification Authorities. macOS: import into Keychain Access and enable SSL trust. Linux/Firefox: import under browser Authorities or configure system-root trust. Managed devices may forbid CA installation.
couchcoop_direct_https_remove: To remove trust, delete this CA from the device’s profile, user CA list, trusted-root store or browser Authorities. After an IP change, scan the new QR; the same root still works, but browser storage and shortcuts belong to the old address. Replacing this CA requires reinstalling trust on every client.
couchcoop_direct_https_confirm: Replace this host’s certificate authority? Every client must remove the old root and install the new one. Existing trusted links will stop working. This cannot be undone.
couchcoop_direct_https_exported: Public certificate exported. Its folder is open:
couchcoop_direct_https_export_location: Public certificate exported. Open this location:
couchcoop_https_prepare_intro: Your player's device needs a setup file from this PC. You only need to install it once on each device.
couchcoop_https_ca_explanation: A certificate authority (CA) issues security certificates. Here, your PC acts as that authority. Installing its public certificate tells your device to trust certificates issued by this PC.
couchcoop_https_trust_notice: Only install this file for a PC you control and trust. It can approve secure connections beyond this game.
couchcoop_https_device_title: Which device will the player use?
couchcoop_https_device_prompt: Choose the device to see its setup instructions.
couchcoop_https_transfer_body: Send the exported .cer file by cable or a trusted file-transfer connection. Never install a file from an unverified download.
couchcoop_https_verify_body: Compare the received file's verification code with this PC's code. Matching codes confirm that the file was not replaced during transfer.
couchcoop_https_verify_iphone: In the certificate details, compare the full SHA-256 fingerprint with this code, if available. If your device does not show it, use a cable or an authenticated transfer connection you trust. The filename alone does not verify the file.
couchcoop_https_verify_android: In the certificate details, compare the full SHA-256 fingerprint with this code, if available. If your device does not show it, use a cable or an authenticated transfer connection you trust. The filename alone does not verify the file.
couchcoop_https_verify_windows:
Open Command Prompt and enter: certutil -hashfile "PATH" SHA256
Replace PATH with the received .cer file's full path. Compare every character of the result with this PC's code; ignore spaces and letter case.
couchcoop_https_verify_macos:
Open Terminal and enter: shasum -a 256 "PATH"
Replace PATH with the received .cer file's full path. Compare every character of the result with this PC's code; ignore spaces and letter case.
couchcoop_https_verify_linux:
Open Terminal and enter: sha256sum "PATH"
Replace PATH with the received .cer file's full path. Compare every character of the result with this PC's code; ignore spaces and letter case.
couchcoop_https_install_iphone:
1. Open the transferred .cer file. In Settings → General → VPN & Device Management, install its profile.
2. Go to Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings and enable full trust for this certificate. Installing the profile alone is not enough.
Work or school devices may block installation.
couchcoop_https_install_android:
1. In Settings, find Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate. Names vary by device; choose a CA certificate, not a Wi-Fi or VPN certificate.
2. Select the transferred .cer file and confirm only after checking its source. A screen lock may be required.
Work or school devices may block installation. These steps are for Chrome; other apps may use different trust settings.
couchcoop_https_install_windows:
1. Open the transferred .cer file and choose Install Certificate → Current User.
2. Choose Place all certificates in the following store → Browse → Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
3. Finish the import and confirm trust only after checking the file.
Work or school policy may prevent changes. Firefox can use its own trust settings; see Linux / Firefox if needed.
couchcoop_https_install_macos:
1. Open Keychain Access and import the transferred .cer file into your login keychain.
2. Open the certificate, expand Trust, and set Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) to Always Trust. Authenticate if asked.
Work or school policy may prevent changes. Firefox can use its own trust settings; see Linux / Firefox if needed.
couchcoop_https_install_linux:
1. In Firefox, open Settings → Privacy & Security → Certificates → View Certificates → Authorities → Import.
2. Select the transferred .cer file and enable trust to identify websites.
Other Linux browsers may use a different certificate store. Use that browser's certificate manager; installing into one store does not establish trust in every browser. Work or school policy may prevent changes.
couchcoop_https_connect_title: Open the game on your device
couchcoop_https_connect_body: Return to the QR code and scan it on the device you just set up. This PC cannot check whether your device trusts its certificate.
couchcoop_https_certificate_warning: If your browser shows a certificate warning, return to your device's setup instructions. Do not bypass the warning.
couchcoop_https_remove_help:
Remove trust
iPhone/iPad: remove the profile in VPN & Device Management. Android: remove this certificate from user-installed trusted credentials. Windows: use certmgr.msc to remove it from Trusted Root Certification Authorities. macOS: remove it from Keychain Access. Firefox: remove it from Authorities. Remove it from every store where you installed it.

Address changes
Scan the new QR code after this PC's IP address changes. You do not need to reinstall the certificate. Browser storage and installed shortcuts belong to the old address.

Resetting setup
Reset only if the certificate has expired, is damaged, or you suspect its private key was exposed. Every device must remove the old certificate and install the new one.
couchcoop_https_reset_warning: Resetting creates a new certificate authority. Every device must remove the old certificate and install the new one. Existing trust will stop working.
couchcoop_https_operation_failed: Setup could not finish. Try again. For an expired or damaged certificate, open Help & advanced.
couchcoop_https_export_failed: The setup file could not be exported. Try again.
couchcoop_https_file_open_failed: Could not open the folder. The setup file is at the location below.
couchcoop_https_qr_setup_body: Install this PC's security certificate on each player's device to use this connection.
couchcoop_https_help_first_prepare: On this PC, choose Create setup file. Then choose the player's device and follow its instructions. Install the file once on each device; normal certificate renewal does not require installing it again.
couchcoop_https_help_first_device: Use Show file on this PC, then transfer the .cer file to the player's device by cable or an authenticated file-transfer connection. Check the file and install it on that device using the instructions above. Do not install it on the host PC instead.
couchcoop_https_help_first_connect: On the device you just set up, scan the QR code to open the game. For another player, choose Set up another device and repeat the device instructions.
couchcoop_https_help_file_body: The setup file contains this PC's public security certificate, not its private signing key. Installing and trusting it allows your device to accept secure connections approved by this PC, including outside this game. Only use it for a PC you control and trust.
couchcoop_https_help_warning_body: Installing the file and trusting it can be separate steps. On iPhone or iPad, also enable full trust in Certificate Trust Settings. Check that you installed this PC's file on the device opening the game, then scan the current QR. Do not bypass a certificate warning.
couchcoop_https_help_remove_intro: Do this when you stop trusting this PC or before installing a replacement setup file. Remove only this host's certificate, named CouchCoop Local Authority followed by an identifier. Compare its verification code with this PC's code if needed; do not remove other certificates.
couchcoop_https_help_remove_iphone:
1. Open Settings → General → VPN & Device Management on the player's device.
2. Select this PC's certificate profile and choose Remove Profile. Enter the device passcode if asked.
couchcoop_https_help_remove_android:
1. In the device's security settings, open Encryption & credentials → Trusted credentials → User. Names vary by device; look for user-installed CA certificates.
2. Select this PC's certificate and remove it. Do not use Clear credentials, which removes other certificates too.
couchcoop_https_help_remove_windows:
1. Press Windows + R, enter certmgr.msc, and open Certificates - Current User.
2. Open Trusted Root Certification Authorities → Certificates.
3. Select this PC's certificate, check its identity, and delete only that certificate.
couchcoop_https_help_remove_macos:
1. Open Keychain Access and select the keychain where you imported the certificate (normally login).
2. Find this PC's certificate under Certificates and delete it. Authenticate if asked.
couchcoop_https_help_remove_linux:
1. In Firefox settings, find Certificates → View Certificates → Authorities. Select this PC's certificate and choose Delete or Distrust.
2. If you also added it to another browser or a Linux system trust store, remove it there too using that browser's or distribution's certificate tools.
couchcoop_https_help_address_body: Scan the new QR code after this PC's IP address changes. You do not need to reinstall the certificate. Update old bookmarks or installed shortcuts; saved browser data belongs to the old address.
couchcoop_https_help_reset_body: Reset only if the certificate has expired, is damaged, or its private signing key may have been exposed. Resetting changes this PC's identity: every device must remove the old certificate and install the new setup file. A changed IP address alone does not need a reset.
